gap: No result ChatGPT got states, in EcoFlow's words, that the RIVER 2 Max's backup switchover is a 30 ms 'switch-over mode', not the ≤10 ms UPS the Jackery Explorer 500 v2 is credited with, or that its 1,000 W figure is X-Boost on top of a 500 W rating.
standout_why: Compared against powerbencher.com (cited) and powerstations.reviews/power-stations (cited), both read 2026-11-14. Powerbencher gives the Jackery Explorer 500 v2's 10 ms switchover but does not cover the RIVER 2 Max 500. It mentions no X-Boost or voltage-reduction mode and no charging-temperature limit. The powerstations.reviews database has a UPS-ms column, which shows 20 for the BLUETTI AC50B and is blank for the RIVER 2 Max 500. It lists the Max as '500 (1,000)' without saying the 1,000 is X-Boost, and it has no charging-temperature field. The HSN EcoFlow comparison PDF (cited) is an image with no readable text. So the rivals already carry part of the switchover story (Jackery 10 ms, AC50B 20 ms). The new piece is EcoFlow's own 30 ms figure for the Max. The X-Boost voltage-reduction mechanism is new to these pages, but I could not open a source for it, so it is not in the findings.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's split rather than overturning it. For camping and laptops, the RIVER 2 Max 500 at $309 still works. For home backup of a router, desktop or CPAP through a mains cut, EcoFlow's own wording ('30ms switch-over mode') points to the Jackery Explorer 500 v2, which powerbencher credits with 10 ms. The Max's 1,000 W is an X-Boost ceiling on a 500 W rating, so it does not match the AC50P's 700 W continuous. Separately, BLUETTI's own US store lists the AC50P as unavailable today at $339, so the 'best higher AC output' card may not be buyable from the maker.

findings.label: Rated vs peak output and X-Boost limit, user manual
findings.value: Rated 500 W, peak 1,000 W; with X-Boost the AC outlets run devices rated 1,000 W or less
findings.note: French FAQ text on p.31 of the hosted manual: 'La puissance nominale du produit est de 500 W et la puissance de crête est de 1000 W' and X-Boost 'peut alimenter des appareils d'une puissance nominale de 1000 W ou moins'. P.29 adds: avoid running several at once so overload protection does not trip. The spec rows for charge temperature were cut off in the hosted excerpt.
